subject: Urgent: Throughput variance & queueing impact — operational pulse
messages:
From: ops@acmepay.com
To: aditya_rao@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@acmepay.com
Date: 2026-09-30T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Unexpected latency and 5xxs during 11:00–12:40 (prod)

Aditya —

We saw a sustained latency spike (median -> 850ms, p95 ~3.2s) and a 5xx increase across our reserved routes between 11:00 and 12:40 PDT. Throughput dropped to ~60% of our expected reserved qps and many inference calls returned 502/503. We attached a short CSV snapshot of request rates and a pared-down error log.

This window is outside our scheduled batch work; our infra team sees sustained queueing on the dedicated GPU pool. Can you confirm whether this was a capacity event on your side or a routing/regression? We need immediate mitigation and an explanation for our SRE and procurement teams.

Attachments: acmepay_kpi_snapshot_20260930.csv

— Alex Chang (Platform Ops), AcmePay
From: aditya_rao@redwood.com
To: ops@acmepay.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-30T08:24:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected latency and 5xxs during 11:00–12:40 (prod)

Alex — thanks for the heads-up and the snapshot. I'm escalating inside Redwood and we'll get you an operational patch ASAP. Initial notes:

- Acknowledged: saw the same p95/5xx signals on our end for AcmePay's reserved routes.
- Different from a code deploy: no infra deploys in that window.
- Suspected cause: transient pooling pressure on the dedicated GPU farm combined with a sudden large model prompt spike from a subset of AcmePay routes (we're still correlating).

Immediate plan (minutes -> 2 hrs):
1) Priyom and his team will instrument detailed logs and push an emergency backstop: route a portion of traffic to the quantized model variant and enable KV-prefetching to reduce token cost and latency.
2) Ops will open a priority burst ticket to shift spare GPU capacity to AcmePay's reserved pool for the next 4 hours.
3) Marissa will coordinate an Ops-to-Ops bridge with your SRE, and procurement if needed, for emergency credits/billing.

Attached: redwood_error_log_1100-1300.txt (sanitized). I'll post updates here. Vivek — flagging for exec awareness due to potential credit/contract impact.

— Aditya Rao | Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
From: priyom_das@redwood.com
To: aditya_rao@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com, dylan_brooks@redwood.com, olga_petrov@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-30T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Unexpected latency and 5xxs during 11:00–12:40 (prod)

Summary of what runtime sees:
- Root signal: queue depth grew on several nodes serving AcmePay's reserved shard; contention at KV cache refills and long tail attention steps triggered timeouts in the proxy layer.
- Correlation: a handful (~3) high-cost routes with very long prompts (>3k tokens) spiked concurrently and consumed >40% of per-node memory/bandwidth; autoscaling thresholds didn't react quickly enough due to config hysteresis.

Immediate mitigation we can run (already executing now):
A) Canary route to quantized-8bit model variant (lower memory and faster kernels) for 30% of traffic — expect median latency improvement ~30–45% and reduced token cost.
B) Short-term token throttles (per-customer rate-limits) for the top 2 heaviest routes; we can tune to avoid customer-visible errors.
C) Manual spill: allocate 4 GPUs from the shared emergency pool to AcmePay's reservation for 2 hours (INF-9021).

Risks: costs will spike while emergency GPUs are in use. There's a small regression risk from model-variant mismatch for certain prompts — we'll enable response-sanity checks for 5 minutes after routing switch to detect drift.

I'll update JIRA INF-9021 with logs and the planned change set.

— Priyom Das | Director, Serving Runtime
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: ops@acmepay.com
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.com, procurement@acmepay.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-30T10:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected latency and 5xxs during 11:00–12:40 (prod) — mutual action plan

Alex —
Thanks for reporting. We own the remediation for the routing/compute side and want to minimize customer impact. Proposed immediate MAP (mutual action plan):

1) Redwood to provision emergency burst (4 GPUs) and engage quantized fallback — target remediation start 10:45 PDT, full effect by 11:00.
2) AcmePay SRE to allow temporary rerouting of 30% of non-critical traffic (we'll mark candidate endpoints).
3) Procurement note: we'll cover emergency overage for this event if the issue is on Redwood's side; please confirm and we'll process credit paperwork after we stabilize.

Can you confirm permission to reroute the non-critical endpoints and confirm procurement contact for the credit paperwork? We are standing by on a bridge.

Attachments: acmepay_kpi_snapshot_20260930.csv (from your team)

— Marissa Cole | Customer Success, Redwood Inference
From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
To: aditya_rao@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com, sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-30T11:16:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected latency and 5xxs during 11:00–12:40 (prod) — exec input

Team — thanks for the rapid triage. I approve the emergency bump (4 GPUs, 2–4 hour window) and activation of the quantized fallback. A few asks for the record and next steps:

- Finance/Rev Ops: Marissa, please document the expected overage and proposed customer credit; keep me in the CC for approvals.
- Product/Eng: Priyom, capture any configuration hysteresis that prevented timely autoscaling and propose one concrete config change we can ship this quarter to reduce the replay risk.
- Sales: Aditya, please draft the external note for AcmePay leadership (CTO + Procurement) summarizing root cause, mitigation, and planned follow-up.

If we need longer capacity, escalate to me directly and I'll coordinate with capacity owners.

— Vivek Kulkarni | VP Sales, Redwood Inference
From: aditya_rao@redwood.com
To: ops@acmepay.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com, sergio_alvarez@redwood.com, dylan_brooks@redwood.com, olga_petrov@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-30T13:45:00-07:00
Subject: Post-mortem snapshot + immediate asks (15:00 exec sync)

Alex —
Thanks for staying on the bridge. Quick status: the canary to quantized-8bit variant reduced median latency from ~850ms -> ~430ms and p95 improved by ~1.6s; emergency GPUs have been attached and queueing cleared. We saw a ~90% reduction in 5xx volume during the stabilized window.

Action items (owners):

- Priyom: create a short mitigation ticket with the autoscale config change and attach the kernel selection logs (INF-9021). Due EOD.
- Aditya (me): executive note to AcmePay CTO + copy to Vivek — will send by 14:30.
- Vivek: available for 15:00 exec sync if needed (15:00–15:20 PDT).

Attachments: redwood_error_log_1100-1300.txt (sanitized), link to INF-9021. We'll follow up with a fuller RCA within 72 hours.

— Aditya Rao | Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
